chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Inform me about the words of Yaqoub (peace be upon him) to his sons: "Go and inquire about Yusuf and his brother." Did he know that he was alive, and that he had been separated from him for twenty years?' He said, 'Yes.'

I said, 'How did he know?' He said, 'Indeed, he supplicated in the pre-dawn hours and asked Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to send down to him the Angel of Death. So Burayza descended to him, and he is the Angel of Death.'

So Burayza said to him, 'What is your need, O Yaqoub?' He said, 'Inform me about the souls. Do you capture them all together or separately?' He said, 'Rather, I capture them separately, soul by soul.'
He said to him, 'So inform me, did the soul of Yusuf pass by you among what passed by you?' He said, 'No.'
Thus Yaqoub came to know that he was alive. So at that time, he said to his sons, 'Go and inquire about Yusuf and his brother.'

key_terms.بُرَيْزَاءُ: Burayza (name of the Angel of Death in this narration)

ai.seo_question: How did Prophet Yaqoub know Yusuf was alive after 20 years?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (as) elucidates the mechanism of Prophet Yaqoub’s (as) knowledge of Yusuf’s survival through a direct inquiry to the Angel of Death, Burayza, during the pre-dawn supplication. The Angel’s response that he captures souls individually ('ruhan ruhan') and had not yet taken Yusuf’s soul served as a definitive sign of life, prompting Yaqoub to send his sons to Egypt. This highlights the Shia understanding of the Angel of Death’s role in conveying specific divine information to the prophets regarding the state of their souls.
